evaluation_title: Scientific Feasibility Assessment for Supervised Disease Classification
recommended_analytical_scope: Retain AgroVision-Mine strictly as an Unsupervised Visual Pattern Mining, Multimodal Data Warehousing, and Reference-Similarity Retrieval Workbench. Do not implement an unsupported end-to-end clinical disease classifier.

justification_factors.evidence: 7 crops (Blueberry, Cherry, Peach, Raspberry, Soybean, Strawberry) contain 100% healthy images; 1 crop (Corn, Potato, Rice, Squash) contains 100% diseased images.
justification_factors.scientific_implication: Any supervised classifier trained to separate Healthy vs Diseased will suffer from severe shortcut learning, memorizing species-level foliar morphology (e.g. Raspberry or Blueberry leaf shape) rather than biological pathology.

justification_factors.factor: Extreme Class Imbalance & Deficient Cell Support
justification_factors.evidence: Class frequencies span 2 orders of magnitude (from N=2 for Tomato Two-Spotted Spider Mite to N=190 for Corn Northern Leaf Blight).
justification_factors.scientific_implication: Statistically sound train/validation/test stratification is impossible for classes with N < 5 (such as Spider Mite with N=2). A test set cannot evaluate precision/recall with N=0 or 1 test instance.

justification_factors.evidence: All 36 Rice images originate from ICAR/OGD lab imaging, while all other 2,560 images originate from PlantDoc crowd-sourced natural field photography.
justification_factors.scientific_implication: Supervised models predicting rice diseases learn dataset source acquisition artifacts (scanner lighting, DPI, background) rather than agricultural disease pathology.

justification_factors.evidence: Features consist of global color moments, Haralick GLCM textures, and binary contour moments, designed for dimensional OLAP and cluster discovery.
justification_factors.scientific_implication: Linear or tree-based classifiers on global descriptors lack localized spatial attention required to distinguish subtle fungal spot lesions from natural foliar venation without high false-positive rates.
